subChunks.title: Data Fetching with TanStack Query
subChunks.hookHtml: Managing server state — data that lives on a server and is fetched, cached, and synchronised — is one of the hardest problems in React. Most teams end up reinventing the same patterns: loading states, error states, caching, refetching, stale data. TanStack Query (formerly React Query) solves all of these with a declarative API that treats server state as a first-class concern, separate from client state.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Client state vs server state

Client state (UI state, selected items, filter values) lives in useState or Zustand. Server state (data from your API) has different characteristics: it's asynchronous, potentially stale, shared across components, and needs cache invalidation. TanStack Query is purpose-built for server state.

Setup

import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';

const queryClient = new QueryClient();

function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Router />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}

useQuery — fetching data

import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

function QuestList() {
  const { data, isLoading, isError, error } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['quests'],
    queryFn: () => fetch('/api/quests').then(r => r.json()),
  });

  if (isLoading) return <p>Loading quests...</p>;
  if (isError) return <p>Error: {error.message}</p>;

  return <ul>{data.map(q => <li key={q.id}>{q.title}</li>)}</ul>;
}

The queryKey is the cache key — the same key from any component gets the same cached data. ['quests', userId] caches per user.

useMutation — modifying data

import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';

function CompleteQuestButton({ questId }) {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();

  const mutation = useMutation({
    mutationFn: (id) =>
      fetch(`/api/quests/${id}/complete`, { method: 'POST' }).then(r => r.json()),

    // After success, invalidate the quests query so it refetches:
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['quests'] });
    },
  });

  return (
    <button
      onClick={() => mutation.mutate(questId)}
      disabled={mutation.isPending}
    >
      {mutation.isPending ? 'Completing...' : 'Complete Quest'}
    </button>
  );
}

Key features

  • Automatic caching: data is cached by queryKey, shared across components, and served instantly on re-mount
  • Background refetching: stale data is refetched in the background when the window regains focus
  • Cache invalidation: invalidateQueries marks a query stale and triggers a refetch
  • Optimistic updates: onMutate callback lets you update the cache before the server responds

Optimistic updates with TanStack Query

const mutation = useMutation({
  mutationFn: completeQuest,
  onMutate: async (questId) => {
    await queryClient.cancelQueries({ queryKey: ['quests'] });
    const previous = queryClient.getQueryData(['quests']);

    // Optimistically update the cache:
    queryClient.setQueryData(['quests'], (old) =>
      old.map(q => q.id === questId ? { ...q, completed: true } : q)
    );

    return { previous }; // Return context for rollback
  },
  onError: (err, questId, context) => {
    queryClient.setQueryData(['quests'], context.previous); // Rollback
  },
  onSettled: () => {
    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['quests'] }); // Sync with server
  },
});

Vex: "TanStack Query does not replace your client state. It replaces your useEffect + useState + fetch boilerplate for server data. Keep UI state in useState or Zustand. Keep server data in TanStack Query. The separation of concerns makes both easier to reason about."

storyBeats.text: A codebase with 30 useEffect fetch calls, each managing its own loading/error/data states. All duplicated. Vex opens a blank store file. 'There is a better way.'

storyBeats.speaker: Vex the Interface Weaver
storyBeats.text: Server state is not client state. It's async. It goes stale. Multiple components need the same data. TanStack Query gives you a cache, automatic background refetching, and declarative loading/error/success states — without any of the useEffect boilerplate. The queryKey is the cache key. The queryFn is your fetch.

storyBeats.speaker: useQuery vs manual fetch

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a quest management UI with TanStack Query:

  • Set up QueryClient and QueryClientProvider in App
  • Build a <QuestList /> using useQuery that fetches from a mock array, handles loading/error/success states, and has data-testid="quest-list"
  • Build a <AddQuestForm /> using useMutation that adds a quest and invalidates the quests query on success
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a full quest management app with TanStack Query: useQuery for listing, useMutation with optimistic updates for completing quests, and another mutation for deleting quests. The optimistic update should mark the quest as completed immediately in the cache, then sync with the mock API. Include proper rollback on error. Add the React Query DevTools panel (ReactQueryDevtools from @tanstack/react-query-devtools).
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between client state and server state, and why TanStack Query exists as a distinct tool from Zustand or Context. Walk through the queryKey system — what does it do, why does the cache key matter, and how does query invalidation work? Then explain optimistic updates: what problem do they solve and how does TanStack Query's onMutate/onError pattern handle rollback?

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the `queryKey` in useQuery?
options: It uniquely identifies the query for caching — the same key from multiple components shares the same cached data
It determines which API endpoint to fetch from
It sets the cache expiration time for the query result
It controls which component triggers the refetch
questions.answer: It uniquely identifies the query for caching — the same key from multiple components shares the same cached data
questions.explanation: The queryKey is TanStack Query's cache key. Two components with useQuery({ queryKey: ['quests'] }) share the same cached data — only one network request is made. Arrays allow parameterisation: ['quests', userId] creates separate cache entries per user. queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['quests'] }) marks all matching queries stale.

options: Marks all matching cached queries as stale and triggers a background refetch if the query has active subscribers
Deletes the cached data immediately from memory
Cancels any in-progress network requests for matching queries
Resets the query to its initial loading state
questions.answer: Marks all matching cached queries as stale and triggers a background refetch if the query has active subscribers
questions.explanation: invalidateQueries marks matching queries as stale. If components are currently subscribed to the query (i.e., mounted), TanStack Query immediately refetches to get fresh data. Components see the cached data instantly, then the background refetch updates them when it resolves. This is the canonical pattern after a mutation: mutate → success → invalidate → fresh data.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of returning a context object from `onMutate` in optimistic updates?
options: To capture the previous cache state before the optimistic update, so it can be restored in onError if the mutation fails
To provide metadata to the onSuccess callback for analytics
To delay the mutation until the context is resolved
To pass additional parameters to the mutationFn
questions.answer: To capture the previous cache state before the optimistic update, so it can be restored in onError if the mutation fails
questions.explanation: onMutate runs before the mutationFn. You save the previous cache state: const previous = queryClient.getQueryData(['quests']). You apply the optimistic update to the cache. You return { previous } as context. If the mutation fails, onError receives this context and calls queryClient.setQueryData(['quests'], context.previous) to roll back. Without the snapshot, you can't recover the previous state on failure.

questions.prompt: Should you store data fetched with TanStack Query in Zustand as well?
options: No — TanStack Query is the cache for server data; duplicating it in Zustand creates sync problems and defeats the cache
Yes — Zustand gives you more control over the data shape
Yes — TanStack Query is only for fetching; Zustand is for storing
Only for data that needs to be persisted to localStorage
questions.answer: No — TanStack Query is the cache for server data; duplicating it in Zustand creates sync problems and defeats the cache
questions.explanation: TanStack Query IS your server data cache. Copying fetched data into Zustand means you have two sources of truth — they diverge when one is updated or invalidated. Use TanStack Query for server state (async, potentially stale, shared). Use Zustand for client state (cart contents, selected items, UI preferences). They complement each other without overlapping.
